title: Several complex variables and Kähler geometry

readme:
# Several complex variables and Kähler geometry

This roadmap has two branches: pseudoconvexity and weighted barpartial solvability leading to the Levi problem, and Hermitian/Kähler harmonic theory leading to vanishing and projective embedding. They share an actual-function complex-Hessian and boundary Levi foundation. Neither branch rebuilds one-variable complex analysis, generic Sobolev theory, analytic sheaf theory or linear Hodge structures.

Use the existing complex normed spaces, manifolds, holomorphic bundles and derivative carriers. The complex differential has factor one-half and the complex-Hessian diagonal factor one-quarter. Defining functions are negative on the selected inside, and their Levi form is restricted to the complex tangent. Its gradient normalization depends on the chosen metric. General plurisubharmonic functions are upper-semicontinuous with possible value minus infinity, not necessarily C2.

Two arbitrary C2 defining functions need not have a C2 ratio, so a smooth-multiplier computation alone does not prove full defining-function independence. Holomorphic pullback uses the actual complex map and its second derivative. Strict positivity can be lost at a critical point. These distinctions have actual-function tests in the companion reader and prototype.

ComplexComparisonPartII owns Weierstrass/coherence, analytic-space and local coherent-cohomology inputs; general Stein extensions stay with that owner. ComplexManifolds PR279 owns realification and holomorphic bundle gluing, with unresolved atlas registration recorded as a gap rather than an invented supplier. PDE owns generic weak-derivative and elliptic machinery. HodgeStructures owns linear Hodge data, while this roadmap realizes those data from compact Kähler cohomology. A real Kähler class is not automatically a rational polarization.

The seven exact stage descriptions below are the build order. The detailed reader develops the 28-node differential foundation and each global target with its remaining proof interfaces. The global statements are not implementation claims. Singular minimal-model theory, arbitrary irregular connections and a general Monge–Ampère existence theorem are not endpoints here.

## Sources

Jiří Lebl, Tasty Bits of Several Complex Variables, version 4.4; Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, 21 June 2012. Exact inspected passages and unclosed source dependencies are recorded below and in the packet. A named endpoint is not evidence that its analytic prerequisites already exist.

stages.title: Complex Hessians and boundary Levi forms
stages.description: Construct the (1,0) part of the actual real Fréchet derivative and the real diagonal of the actual complex Hessian, using the existing real bilinear second derivative. Prove the mixed-derivative and affine-line Laplacian comparisons with their factors one-half and one-quarter, and the scalar, product and holomorphic chain rules. Define the complex tangent as the existing kernel of the complex differential. On a regular zero level with the convention rho<0 inside, construct the operator-norm-normalized tangent Levi diagonal. Prove its precise comparison for a GIVEN C2 nonzero multiplier and its orientation sign. Do not assume that arbitrary C2 defining functions have a C2 ratio. The full coordinate Hermitian polarization and general C2 defining-function independence are explicit closure work, with the latter using the implicit-function/level-curve argument. No assertion about a total derivative at a nonsmooth function replaces regularity.

stages.title: Holomorphic functions and local analytic geometry
stages.description: Work on actual finite-dimensional complex normed spaces and open sets, using existing holomorphic/analytic predicates. Prove the several-variable Cauchy formulas on polydiscs, power-series comparison, separate holomorphy implies joint holomorphy, and the local holomorphic inverse/rank consequences with their precise hypotheses, only beyond the verified baseline. Reuse one-variable contour and normal-family theory instead of reconstructing it. Develop analytic continuation and the Hartogs extension theorem for an open connected Omega in C^n, n>=2, with compact K contained in Omega and Omega minus K connected: a holomorphic function there extends uniquely to Omega. Import convergent germs, Weierstrass preparation/division, coherence and nonreduced analytic-space carriers from ComplexComparisonPartII:C0 and its identified extension; apply them to analytic zero loci, regular loci and local parametrization. Do not identify an analytic subspace with its reduced zero set or claim one-variable holes are removable.

stages.title: Plurisubharmonic functions and pseudoconvexity
stages.description: Define general plurisubharmonic functions as upper-semicontinuous functions with values in R union minus infinity whose restrictions to complex lines are subharmonic or identically minus infinity. They are not required to be C2. Prove their basic maximum, decreasing-limit, holomorphic pullback, convex increasing composition and local regularization properties with the necessary boundedness/noncollapse qualifications. Prove the C2 criterion from the actual affine-line Laplacian and the one-variable subharmonic Laplacian characterization, including the source proof exercises. Relate psh exhaustion, holomorphic convexity/domain-of-holomorphy and boundary notions through precisely stated theorems, not by treating them as identical definitions. For a C2 regular boundary, prove intrinsic defining-function independence without a false C2-ratio assertion, then the boundary Levi criterion and strict local defining-function/exhaustion constructions. Keep pointwise Levi positivity separate from a global exhaustion. Test balls, halfspaces, product domains, the dimension-one tangent boundary and a same-side defining function whose normal Hessian is negative.

stages.title: The weighted barpartial equation and the Levi problem
stages.description: On pseudoconvex domains in C^n construct the actual barpartial operators on complex forms, their weak realizations and weighted Hilbert adjoints with specified graph domains. Establish the integration-by-parts, basic estimate, domain-density and exhaustion steps before using Hilbert duality to solve barpartial. As a fixed acceptance theorem, for smooth strictly plurisubharmonic phi, a distributionally barpartial-closed (0,1) form g with finite integral of |g|^2 exp(-phi) divided by the smallest complex-Hessian eigenvalue has an L2 solution f with that integral as the squared-norm bound. Here |g|^2 is the sum of squares of the dbarz coefficients and the measure is Euclidean Lebesgue measure. Reconcile the scalar statement with Demailly VIII (6.5), which is a theorem on (n,q) forms; Euclidean trivialization has zero canonical curvature. On curved manifolds keep the canonical-bundle/Ricci contribution rather than silently relabel (n,q) as (0,q). Prove the analytic exhaustion/holomorphic-separation steps of the Levi problem and Stein applications. Local Cousin, coherent sheaf and Cartan A/B theorems stay with ComplexComparisonPartII:C0–C1 and its general-Stein extension; route the new analytic estimates there without a proof cycle. No general smooth-boundary regularity of solutions is asserted from the interior L2 estimate alone.

stages.title: Hermitian bundles and Kähler geometry
stages.description: Use existing complex-manifold and holomorphic vector-bundle carriers, including the actual realification and bundle chart interfaces owned by ComplexManifolds PR279. Construct type decomposition of smooth forms, partial/barpartial and their identities, the local Dolbeault resolution and its comparison with existing sheaf cohomology. Introduce Hermitian metrics and the unique Chern connection whose (0,1) part is the holomorphic structure and which is metric-compatible, using any verified generic connection API rather than a replacement bundle. Pin curvature and positivity conventions: for a local line metric exp(-phi), the real curvature form is i partial barpartial phi; the geometric Kähler form is a real closed positive (1,1) form and the standard Euclidean form is (i/2) sum dz_j wedge dbarz_j. Prove local potentials and changes of frame, tensor/dual curvature, and the distinction between Griffiths and Nakano positivity. A positive pointwise two-form is not assumed closed. The analytic line-bundle and manifold structure is not rebuilt from an unrelated algebraic KaehlerDifferential carrier.

stages.title: Compact Kähler Hodge theory
stages.description: For a compact Kähler manifold without boundary, construct the actual adjoints and Hodge Laplacians on forms, prove the Kähler commutator identities and Delta_d=2 Delta_barpartial in the stated normalization, and establish harmonic representatives by the generic compact vector-bundle elliptic theory. That elliptic theory needs its genuine owner extension; a scalar domain estimate does not discharge it. Prove the ddbar lemma, the metric-independent Hodge decomposition and conjugation, degeneration of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence, and the Lefschetz decomposition, hard Lefschetz theorem and Hodge-Riemann signs. Export the resulting geometric Hodge structure into the existing HodgeStructures carrier on integral cohomology modulo torsion or the chosen rational lattice, using the actual de Rham/Betti comparison. A general real Kähler class supplies real Lefschetz data; assert a rational polarization only with a rational Kähler class. Generic sheaf/derived-cohomology operations, linear Hodge structures and their semisimplicity are imports, not new constructions here.

stages.title: Positivity, vanishing and projective embedding
stages.description: On a compact Kähler manifold X of complex dimension n, prove the Bochner-Kodaira-Nakano identity for the actual Chern connection and harmonic forms, including the curvature operator and its bidegree signs. Deduce the line-bundle Akizuki-Nakano vanishing H^{p,q}(X,L)=0 for a positive holomorphic line bundle L and p+q>n; in particular H^q(X,K_X tensor L)=0 for q>0. Positivity is a geometric hypothesis, not the presence of an arbitrary Hermitian metric. Construct sections of sufficiently high positive powers that separate points and tangent directions, make the resulting projective map, and prove it is a holomorphic embedding. Global finite generation alone does not imply an embedding. Finish Kodaira embedding and the equivalence between projectivity and a positive line bundle in the stated compact setting, keeping integral Chern classes and the 2pi normalization explicit. Use projective GAGA/Chow from ComplexComparisonPartII after the analytic embedding, never as a circular premise for constructing it. General singular vanishing and the full minimal-model programme are outside these smooth targets.
